title: Chelfray (Iraqi lamb, potato and pepper stew)

ingredients.name: salt and black pepper to taste

steps: Heat the oil in a heavy pot and brown the lamb cubes on all sides.
Add the onion and cook for a few minutes until softened.
Stir in the baharat, salt and black pepper, then add the tomatoes, bell pepper and hot peppers.
Add the potatoes and just enough water to come halfway up the ingredients.
Cover and cook on low heat for 1 to 1.5 hours until the lamb is tender and the sauce is thick.
Serve with rice or fresh bread.

title: Kahi (Iraqi flaky pastry with cream and syrup)

ingredients.name: vegetable oil, plus more for frying
thick cream (kaymak/geymar, clotted cream or mascarpone)

steps: Knead the flour, salt, water and 2 tablespoons of oil into a soft dough, cover, and rest for 30 minutes.
Divide into 6 balls and roll each as thinly as you can, brushing generously with oil.
Fold each sheet into a square, brushing oil between the layers so they separate as they fry.
Fry the squares in a shallow layer of hot oil for 1 to 2 minutes per side until puffed, golden and crisp.
Drain on paper towels and serve warm with a spoonful of cream and a drizzle of date syrup or honey.

title: Kleicha (Iraqi date-filled cookies)

ingredients.name: egg yolk beaten with a little milk, for glaze

steps: Mix the flour, yeast, sugar, half the cardamom and salt. Add the melted butter and rub it into the flour.
Add the warm milk and bring the mixture into a soft dough, kneading briefly, then cover and rest for 1 hour.
Mash the date paste with the tablespoon of butter and the rest of the cardamom until smooth.
Divide the dough into walnut-sized pieces, flatten each into a disc, put a teaspoon of date filling in the centre, and close the dough around it.
Press each ball into a flat round and mark the top with a fork or small tongs.
Brush with the egg glaze and bake at 180 C for 20 to 25 minutes until golden. Cool on a rack.

title: Kubba halab (Iraqi fried rice dumplings with spiced meat)

ingredients.name: oil, plus oil for deep frying

steps: Boil the rice in plenty of water until very soft and slightly overcooked, then drain and mash it while hot with the flour, turmeric and a pinch of salt until it forms a sticky paste. Chill for 30 minutes.
Brown the onion in 2 tablespoons of oil, add the meat and cook until it loses its raw colour, then stir in the almonds, baharat, parsley, salt and pepper. Cool the filling.
With wet hands, take a ball of rice paste, flatten it in your palm, put a spoonful of filling in the middle, and close it into an oval, sealing the seam well.
Heat oil for deep frying to about 175 C and fry the dumplings in small batches for 4 to 5 minutes until deep golden and crisp.
Drain on paper towels and serve hot with lemon or amba.

title: Masgouf (Iraqi grilled whole fish)

ingredients.name: whole carp, sea bass or sea bream, cleaned and split open along the belly or back (butterflied)
onions, sliced into rings, for serving

steps: Open the fish flat so it lies like a book and pat it dry. Make a few shallow cuts in the thick part of the flesh.
Mix the olive oil, tamarind paste, turmeric and salt and rub it over both sides of the fish. Leave it for 30 minutes.
Heat a charcoal grill or a very hot oven grill. Place the fish flesh-side towards the heat first and cook for 10 to 12 minutes.
Turn the fish and cook the skin side for another 10 to 15 minutes until the skin is crisp and the thickest part flakes easily.
Move the fish to a board, drizzle with a little more oil, and serve at once with onion rings, tomato, lemon wedges and bread.

title: Quzi (Iraqi slow-cooked lamb on spiced rice)

ingredients.name: lamb shoulder or leg, on the bone, in large pieces
baharat (or a mix of allspice, cinnamon and black pepper)

steps: Put the lamb, onions, cinnamon, cardamom and a good pinch of salt in a heavy pot with water to cover and bring to the boil, skimming off the foam.
Reduce the heat, cover, and simmer very gently for 2 to 2.5 hours until the meat is falling off the bone. Strain and keep the broth.
Fry the almonds and raisins briefly in half the ghee until golden and plump, and set aside.
Fry the carrots in the remaining ghee for a few minutes, add the baharat and the rice and stir for a minute.
Pour in about 700 ml of the hot lamb broth, add the peas and salt, bring to a boil, cover, and cook on the lowest heat for 15 to 18 minutes. Rest for 10 minutes off the heat.
Pile the rice on a large platter, lay the lamb on top, and scatter with the fried almonds and raisins.

title: Samoon (Iraqi diamond-shaped bread)
steps: Mix the flour, yeast, sugar and salt, then add the water and oil and knead for about 10 minutes until smooth and elastic.
Cover and let the dough rise in a warm place until doubled, about 1.5 hours.
Divide into 6 pieces, shape each into a ball, rest for 10 minutes, then roll or stretch into an oval about 15 cm long and pinch the two ends into points to make a diamond shape.
Place on a floured tray and let them rise again for 20 minutes.
Put a tray of hot water in the bottom of the oven for steam and bake the bread at 240 C for 12 to 15 minutes until golden with a crisp crust.
Eat warm with kebabs, hummus or stews.

title: Tepsi baytinijan (Iraqi baked aubergine and tomato casserole)
steps: Salt the aubergine slices and leave them for 20 minutes, then rinse and pat dry.
Fry the aubergine and potato slices in batches in oil until golden on both sides and drain them on paper towels.
Soften the onions in a little oil, add the garlic and cook for a minute. If you like, brown 300 g minced lamb with them at this stage.
Dissolve the tomato paste and baharat in the hot water with salt and pepper to make a loose sauce.
Layer the potatoes, aubergine, onion mixture and tomato slices in a deep baking dish, finishing with tomatoes, and pour the sauce over.
Bake at 190 C for 35 to 40 minutes until bubbling and the vegetables are tender, then serve with rice or flatbread.
